description: Japchae Sweet Potato Glass Noodles is a beloved Korean dish featuring chewy sweet potato glass noodles stir-fried with an array of colorful vegetables and often beef or mushrooms, all tossed in a savory soy-sesame sauce. This vibrant and flavorful Korean pasta offers a delightful balance of textures and tastes, making it a popular choice for celebrations and everyday meals alike. It's a healthy and satisfying dish that perfectly showcases the harmony of Korean cuisine.

ingredients.notes: thinly sliced, or shiitake mushrooms for vegetarian

instructions.title: Prepare the Noodles
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add the sweet potato glass noodles and cook for 8-10 minutes, or until translucent and chewy. Drain the noodles and rinse them under cold water to prevent sticking. Cut them into shorter, manageable lengths using kitchen shears. Toss with 1 tablespoon of sesame oil to keep them from clumping.

instructions.title: Blanch and Season Spinach
instructions.text: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for about 30 seconds until wilted. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking, then squeeze out excess water. In a small bowl, season the spinach with 1 teaspoon soy sauce and 1/2 teaspoon minced garlic. Set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare and Cook Vegetables
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the julienned carrots, sliced onion, and bell peppers. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp. Transfer the cooked vegetables to a large mixing bowl.

instructions.title: Marinate and Cook Beef
instructions.text: In a small bowl, marinate the thinly sliced beef with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1/2 tablespoon sugar, 1/2 teaspoon minced garlic, and a pinch of black pepper for 10 minutes. In the same wok, add a little more vegetable oil if needed. Cook the marinated beef until browned and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes. Add to the mixing bowl with the cooked vegetables.

instructions.title: Make the Japchae Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 1.5 tablespoons sugar, 2 tablespoons sesame oil, and remaining 2 teaspoons minced garlic. This will be your Japchae sauce.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Add the prepared noodles and seasoned spinach to the large mixing bowl with the vegetables and beef. Pour the Japchae sauce over all the ingredients. Using clean hands or tongs, gently toss everything together until well combined and the noodles are evenly coated with the sauce. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: For perfectly chewy noodles, make sure not to overcook them. Rinsing with cold water immediately after boiling is crucial to stop the cooking process and prevent stickiness.
Cook each ingredient separately. This traditional Korean method ensures each component retains its unique texture and flavor, preventing the dish from becoming mushy.
Japchae is delicious both warm and at room temperature. It makes excellent leftovers and can be gently reheated in a pan or microwave, adding a splash of water or sesame oil if it seems dry.
